caption:
Mountain biking in Costa Rica means accepting that some slopes were never meant to be ridden. Our mountain roads and cattle paths don't believe in switchbacks; they climb the ridges directly, chasing the shortest line to the sky. When the grass is damp and the gradient passes twenty-five percent, the smartest gear is simply standing up and walking your bike. Here, the transition from rider to hiker isn't a defeat—it is a quiet, necessary conversation with the terrain. Lungs burn, shoes slip on the wet clay, and you realize that the pace is always decided by the mountain. The reward is the silence at the top, where the ridge finally levels out and the cloud forest opens up before you.
